hyps.why: From very small learning rates, increasing the rate fixes undertraining within the fixed epoch budget.
At already large learning rates, further increases push Adam into divergence and accuracy collapse.
Lowering an excessively large learning rate rescues unstable training.
Large batches give fewer, less noisy updates, so they benefit more from bigger steps.
Tiny batches combined with higher learning rates produce noisy, unstable updates.
With a small learning rate, larger batches reduce the number of updates and leave the model undertrained.
At high learning rates, larger batches smooth gradients and stabilize training.
When L2 is already strong, increasing it further causes underfitting, while at tiny alpha it is nearly neutral.
Narrow networks are capacity-limited, so adding units helps most there, with diminishing returns at large widths.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units at large learning rates.
